children: U.S. equities pushed lower on Wednesday as oil kept climbing, with Brent crude (
) breaking above $100 a barrel while U.S.–Iran tensions in the Middle East continued to weigh on sentiment.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
Treasury yields climb on expanded buyback:

Wednesday after the Treasury Department said it will repurchase up to $6 billion of longer-dated notes in Thursday's operation, tripling the size of its last long-end buyback. The 2-year yield rose 2 basis points to 4.42%, its highest level since July 2024, while the benchmark 10-year yield added 5 basis points to 4.84%, a level not seen since November 2023. The 30-year yield also moved higher, gaining about 4 basis points near 5.29%.

Front-month Brent crude for November delivery climbed 3.3% to $101.13/bbl, while front-month Nymex crude jumped 3.2% to $96.02/bbl. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply during the recent escalation, falling from roughly 8 million barrels per day during the last week of August to only 1 million barrels per day this week, according to Rystad Energy.

Hubinger said Anthropic is "trying its best" but does not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and is not clearly on track to do so. Anthropic's latest risk report upgraded the risk from misalignment in high-stakes settings to "low" from its previous "very low" assessment, noting the company has observed misaligned behavior from its models in difficult tasks.
Managed care stocks fall on cost warnings:
Managed care  stocks declined on Wednesday after CVS Health

said at the Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference that the company continues to face elevated medical costs. Notable decliners include UnitedHealth, Humana, Clover Health, Alignment Healthcare, Centene, Oscar Health, Elevance Health, and Molina Healthcare. "Absolute healthcare costs are still much higher than any of us would like to see them," said Steve Nelson, president of CVS's Aetna unit, adding that it is "very much at the front of our large purchasers' minds."
